_note: Seeded 2026-09-14 from direct repository inspection during /jrs-init. Counts are FACT as at the commit recorded in PROGRAM_STATE.json. Rights and status fields are carried from the authoritative baseline in docs/enterprise-diligence/ and are NOT re-derived here.

claims.claim: Mean reviewer accuracy 83.9% (95% CI 72.7 to 95.1, n=16, 384 graded reads)
claims.limitations: Accuracy range 37.5 to 100 percent; pre-registered reliability criterion NOT met. Both are published alongside.
Balanced 24-record constructed corpus; supports detectability, not a population rate.

claims.claim: A deficit rate for real-world records
claims.limitations: NOT DERIVABLE. A 50/50 constructed corpus cannot produce a population estimate. Requested three times; refused each time.
claims.enforcement_reason: 'deficit rate' appears in the research records describing what is NOT claimed

claims.limitations: Functional operation is not validation. CORRECTED 2026-09-14: the self-declaration exists ONLY in api/review-engine.js and api/v1/review-engine.js. api/review.js carries none and is the endpoint behind index.html, training.html and review-engine.html.
claims.enforcement_reason: 'validated' appears in the version string 0.1.0-validation and in negations

claims.claim: JRS is certification, accreditation or a credential
claims.limitations: Explicitly disclaimed on compliance.html and in the guides.
claims.enforcement_reason: 'certification' appears in training copy describing what JRS is not

claims.claim: The 70% figure is a pre-registered threshold that was CLEARED
claims.limitations: It is a success threshold for human detection, not a deficit rate. Both public occurrences state it as cleared.

claims.claim: JRS output is admissible in court
claims.limitations: NOT ESTABLISHED. Admissibility is a legal determination (Rule 8).
claims.enforcement_reason: 'admissible' appears in disclaimers stating admissibility is not established

claims.limitations: NOT ESTABLISHED, and the banned-language list in Section 24 covers it.
claims.enforcement_reason: 'liability' appears in terms and disclaimers as the thing NOT promised

claims.claim: JRS satisfies a statute, regulation or standard
claims.limitations: Rule 9. No regulatory crosswalk has been performed.

claims.claim: JRS is an industry standard or has industry recognition
claims.limitations: NOT ESTABLISHED. No standards body, no DOI, no publisher record for any JRS output.
claims.enforcement_reason: 'industry standard' appears in copy disclaiming the status

claims.claim: Real-world effectiveness of JRS in production use
claims.limitations: No real-case criterion validity study exists. The site says so.

claims.claim: Sixteen experts across eleven countries read a balanced 24-record corpus cold
claims.limitations: Constructed corpus, deliberately balanced. Supports detectability only.

claims.claim: The call is stateless / no retention or data-residency obligation arises
claims.public_use: NEVER. It is false of the code and the third limb is a legal conclusion.
claims.limitations: Record TEXT is genuinely not stored. That accurate narrower claim is C-14. The engine writes engine_reviews on every authenticated call.
claims.known_live_occurrence: openapi.json info.summary and info.description. B-016, COUNSEL REVIEW REQUIRED, correction drafted and UNAPPLIED.

claims.claim: The record text you submit is never stored
claims.public_use: Permitted. It is the accurate narrower form of C-13.
claims.limitations: True of the RECORD TEXT only. Model output ABOUT the record is stored and is covered by C-15. input_preview stopped being written 2026-08-14.
claims.evidence: api/v1/review-engine.js logReview payload carries no record text

claims.claim: Model output about the record is kept for 90 days and then removed; the evaluation record is retained
claims.status: DEMONSTRATED AS POLICY, NOT AS EXECUTED BEHAVIOUR
claims.public_use: Permitted in the three-category form only.
claims.limitations: BD-10/BD-12/BD-13. The policy module COMPUTES; it does not delete. NO EXPIRY HAS RUN ANYWHERE and engine_reviews holds zero rows. A bare '90 days' is prohibited because it reads as the whole row being deleted.
claims.evidence: lib/retention/policy.js days:90; privacy.html and security.html disclosure

claims.claim: The Manifest is authenticated / proves authorship or authenticity
claims.limitations: integrity is a sha256 hash plus a canonicalization id. There is no signing key and no authentication mechanism. A hash is not a signature. It does not establish who produced the manifest.

claims.claim: The canonicalization is RFC 8785 / JCS compliant
claims.limitations: The identifier is jrs-dev-canon-1, deliberately NOT claimed compliant, because it has not been verified against the RFC's test vectors.

claims.claim: Responses submitted through finding.html are not displayed publicly
claims.status: PROMISED AT COLLECTION; NOT YET TRUE IN THE DATABASE
claims.public_use: It is already published on finding.html and must remain honoured.
claims.limitations: B-017. The export row is removed and no page reads the table, but the anon SELECT GRANT REMAINS until a production operation revokes it. The page projection is not the control; the grant is.
claims.evidence: finding.html promise; supabase-ALL.sql read policy; BD-14

claims.limitations: PRODUCTION-VERIFIED CONTROLS: NONE. Every remediation is development evidence. Development evidence does not become production evidence by assertion.

_evidence_chain_rule: CLAIM -> EVIDENCE -> LIMITATION -> RIGHTS -> REGULATORY IMPLICATION -> APPROVAL (Section 24)
_extended_2026_09_17: Extended, not rebuilt. The 12 seeded claims are unchanged. Added: (a) a representation dimension per claim, because a claim is controlled only where it is SAID, and B-016 is a claim that was correct on every HTML surface and false in JSON; (b) the claims that arose from BD-10 to BD-16, B-016 and B-017, which post-date the 2026-09-14 seed. Surface classes: HTML = deployed pages; JSON = published machine artifacts including openapi.json; DOCS = diligence records; CODE = executable.
_representation_rule: CLAIM -> SOURCE -> EVIDENCE -> AUTHORITY -> VERSION -> LIMITATION -> REPRESENTATION. A claim is not controlled by being written down once. It is controlled where it is SAID. The 2026-09-15 claims sweep removed a data-handling proposition from ten HTML pages and left it live in openapi.json, because the sweep read HTML. Every claim below names the surface classes it may and may not appear on.
_enforcement_rule: Each PROHIBITED claim declares how it is enforced. TWO MODES, and the split is a recorded decision, not a convenience. 'pattern' is for phrases with NO innocent form, where an automated check is reliable. 'human_review' is for terms that appear legitimately inside negations, disclaimers, version strings, quotations and historical references -- for these an automated scan was DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT on 2026-09-15, because a naive substring check flagged 'validated' in the version string '0.1.0-validation' and in the phrase 'is NOT established as validated', and flagged 'legally defensible' inside 'does not determine whether ... legally defensible'. That finding recorded: false-positive governance is worse than none. B-016 is new evidence for the NARROW class only -- a claim escaped into JSON because the human scan read HTML -- and it does not overturn the wider decision.
